addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- amazon-bedrock: Builds generative AI applications on Amazon Bedrock. Covers model invocation (Converse API, InvokeModel), RAG with Knowledge Bases, Bedrock Agents, Guardrails, and AgentCore. Use when invoking models, setting up Knowledge Bases, creating agents, applying guardrails, deploying to AgentCore, troubleshooting Bedrock errors (ThrottlingException, AccessDeniedException), or choosing models (Claude, Llama, [infra], Titan). ALSO USE for prompt caching setup and debugging, quota health checks and throttling diagnosis, cost attribution and tracking, migrating between Claude model generations (4.5 to 4.6 to 4.7), chunking strategies, API selection (Converse vs InvokeModel), guardrail capabilities, and model selection. Also covers AgentCore Payments setup (x402, microtransactions, Payment Manager, Connector, Instrument, Coinbase CDP, Stripe Privy, 402 Payment Required, pay for content, paid endpoint, agent payments). NOT for custom model training, Rekognition, or Comprehend.
- aws-billing-and-cost-management: Analyze AWS costs, find savings, manage budgets, evaluate Savings Plans and Reserved Instances, right-size EC2/Lambda/RDS/EBS with Compute Optimizer, look up service pricing, query CUR with Athena, detect cost anomalies, scope costs to billing views, and monitor Free Tier usage. Triggers on: AWS bill, cost analysis, reduce spend, savings plan, reserved instance, right-size, budget alert, cost optimization, pricing, free tier, cost anomaly, CUR, cost audit, billing view, billing view ARN.

Applies when creating APIs, selecting Building Blocks (KVStore, DistributedTable, Database, AuthBasic, AuthCognito, Realtime, AsyncJob, FileBucket, etc.), running local development, or deploying AWS Blocks applications. Also covers AWS Blocks topics with validated, version-specific patterns that prevent common mistakes. Triggers when user mentions AWS Blocks; project has aws-blocks/ directory; code imports @aws-blocks packages.
- aws-cdk: Authors, deploys, and troubleshoots AWS infrastructure using CDK with TypeScript or Python. Covers best practices, stack architecture, and construct patterns. Always use when writing CDK constructs, bootstrapping environments, running cdk deploy/synth/diff, fixing CDK or CloudFormation errors, planning stack structure, importing existing resources, resolving drift, or refactoring stacks without resource replacement.
- aws-cloudformation: Author, validate, and troubleshoot AWS CloudFormation templates. Covers template authoring with secure defaults, pre-deployment validation (cfn-lint, cfn-guard, change sets), and root-cause diagnosis of failed stacks using CloudFormation events and CloudTrail correlation.
- aws-containers: Deploys and operates containerized workloads on ECS, Fargate, and ECR. Covers task definitions, Fargate services, ECR repository setup and lifecycle policies, ECS Exec debugging, service scaling, deployment strategies, load balancer integration, and logging configuration. Use when deploying, debugging, or optimizing containers on AWS. ALSO USE for container deployment options (ECS vs ECS Express Mode), networking modes, health check troubleshooting, OOM errors, secrets injection, blue/green deployments, ECR image management, and App Runner sunset guidance and migration. NOT for Kubernetes, EKS, or CI/CD pipelines.
- aws-messaging-and-streaming: Guides use of AWS messaging and streaming services. Covers Amazon SQS, Amazon SNS, Amazon EventBridge, Amazon MQ, Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon Data Firehose, Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, and Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK). Use when implementing messaging and streaming patterns.
- aws-observability: Builds, configures, debugs, and optimizes AWS observability with CloudWatch (Log Insights, Metrics, Alarms, Dashboards, EMF), X-Ray, CloudTrail, and ADOT (AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry), AND enables/onboards services to Application Signals using ADOT auto-instrumentation SDKs. Covers Log Insights queries, alarms (metric, composite, anomaly), dashboards, custom metrics/EMF, X-Ray tracing and sampling, ADOT collector config, CloudTrail auditing, and end-to-end Application Signals enablement via ADOT SDKs (CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on, CloudWatch Agent IAM, OTLP endpoints, ServiceEvents, Dynamic Instrumentation), breakpoint and snapshot in Dynamic Instrumentation, live data capture in running service, debug without redeploying. Applies to CloudWatch, alarms, dashboards, EMF, X-Ray, traces, CloudTrail,  ADOT, monitoring, synthetics/canaries, OR enabling/onboarding/instrumenting a service for Application Signals. Not for app logging or security threat detection.
- aws-sdk-js-v3-usage: AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 development patterns. Use when writing JavaScript or TypeScript code that uses AWS services via @aws-sdk/* packages (aws-sdk-js-v3), or when asked about schemas, runtime validation, serialization, or code generation in the context of the JS/TS AWS SDK.
- aws-sdk-python-usage: AWS SDK for Python (boto3/botocore) development patterns. You MUST use this skill when writing Python code that uses AWS services via boto3 or botocore. This includes creating service clients or resources, configuring sessions and credentials, handling errors with ClientError, using paginators and waiters, S3 file transfers and presigned URLs, DynamoDB table operations, and any boto3/botocore client configuration. Use this skill whenever Python code imports boto3 or botocore, or when the user asks about AWS operations in Python.
- aws-sdk-swift-usage: AWS SDK for Swift development patterns. Use when writing Swift code that uses AWS services via aws-sdk-swift package.
- aws-serverless: Builds, deploys, manages, debugs, configures, and optimizes serverless applications on AWS using Lambda, API Gateway, Step Functions, EventBridge, and SAM/CDK. Covers cold starts, CORS debugging, event source mappings, troubleshooting, concurrency, SnapStart, Powertools, function URLs, EventBridge Scheduler, Lambda layers, and production readiness. Triggers on mentions of Lambda, API Gateway, Step Functions, SAM templates, CDK serverless stacks, DynamoDB stream triggers, SQS event sources, cold starts, timeouts, 502/504 errors, throttling, concurrency, CORS, Powertools, or any event-driven architecture on AWS, even without the word "serverless." - cso: Chief Security Officer mode. (gstack)
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

- review: Pre-landing PR review. (gstack)

Activates when a developer needs to authenticate to AWS for local development, when an AWS operation fails due to missing or expired credentials, or when someone asks about setting up AWS access. Triggers: "set up AWS", "configure AWS", "aws login", "get credentials", "authenticate", "session expired", "token expired", "no credentials", "AccessDeniedException" with no configured credentials.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.

1	---
2	redu_schema: 2
3	repo: https://github.com/Budibase/budibase
4	plan:
5	  tool: deploy_compose
6	  image: budibase/apps:3.41.3 (plus worker, proxy, database, minio, redis)
7	  port: 10000
8	  vm: m1.large
9	  flavor_id: "4"
10	  database: none. Budibase's system of record is CouchDB, which redu does not offer managed, so it runs on the app VM on a named volume
11	  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0486
12	bootstrap:
13	  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
14	  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
15	  source: budibase
16	quirks:
17	  - "⛔⛔ READ THIS BEFORE SIZING OR PROMISING ANYTHING: THERE IS NO MANAGED DATABASE IN THIS RECIPE, AND THAT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Budibase keeps every app definition, every internal table row, every user and every setting in COUCHDB, and redu has no managed CouchDB. Its files, attachments and built app bundles live in MINIO, and redu has no managed object store either. Both therefore run as containers on the app VM, on named volumes. Consequence, and say it to the user in these words BEFORE they approve: this is the entry in the library whose data does NOT survive the VM. A source re-upload keeps named volumes; delete_deployment, or losing the VM, takes the apps with it. Budibase's own workspace export and a scheduled couchdb dump are the backup story, not the platform."
18	  - "⛔ WHAT REDU CAN AND CANNOT REPLACE, SO NOBODY RE-DERIVES IT. CouchDB: NOT replaceable, no managed equivalent, and charts/budibase/values.yaml:883-890 says upstream does not support any other CouchDB image anyway. MinIO: NOT replaceable here, though values.yaml:806-826 shows it can point at an external S3-compatible bucket if the user brings one. Redis: replaceable with a redu managed Redis at +GBP 0.0174/hr, and NOT worth it by default, because it holds sessions, caches and the automation queue rather than a system of record; losing it costs a re-login. LiteLLM's Postgres: replaceable, but this recipe deletes LiteLLM entirely, see the next quirk, so there is nothing left to point at a managed database."
19	  - "DELETE litellm-service AND litellm-db. Two independent pieces of upstream evidence say the AI gateway is optional: charts/budibase/values.yaml:725-727 ships services.litellm.enabled FALSE by default, and packages/server/src/startup/index.ts:48-52 skips the LiteLLM readiness wait entirely when LITELLM_MASTER_KEY is unset. A third says it would be useless anyway on an unlicensed self-host: packages/pro/src/constants/licenses.ts gives SELF_FREE_LICENSE customAIConfigurations 0 and budibaseAICredits 0. So remove both services, remove them from every depends_on, and do NOT set LITELLM_MASTER_KEY or LITELLM_URL. ⚠️ If you set LITELLM_MASTER_KEY with no LiteLLM running, the app container blocks about 30 seconds at boot waiting for a readiness check that cannot succeed, then carries on: a slow boot that looks like a hang. Keeping LiteLLM also means a postgres:16 container on the app VM or a managed Postgres at +GBP 0.0174/hr, which changes the quote, so it is the user's call and not yours."
20	  - "⛔ PIN EVERY IMAGE. THE UPSTREAM COMPOSE PINS ONLY TWO OF EIGHT. budibase/apps, budibase/worker, budibase/proxy, minio/minio and redis are all written with no tag, which is :latest, on a file people copy verbatim. Registry-checked pins on 2026-08-17: budibase/apps:3.41.3, budibase/worker:3.41.3, budibase/proxy:3.41.3 (all published 2026-08-04, matching the newest GitHub release), budibase/database:2.1.0 (its newest, from 2026-03-13), minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z (the newest community MinIO tag, and it is from 2025), redis:7.4.10. Keep the three Budibase images on the SAME version as each other. ⚠️ Ignore the v3.42.0-cloud tags: they are the hosted build, they have no matching GitHub release, and they are not what self-hosting docs describe."
21	  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR, AND WHEN. SET BB_ADMIN_USER_EMAIL AND [REDACTED:value] IN THE ENV BEFORE THE FIRST BOOT, AND THIS IS THE ONE THING YOU MUST NOT SKIP. With them set, packages/server/src/startup/index.ts:199-238 creates the admin account inside the app container's startup, before redu's hostname is even routing, which is the safe-by-construction case. WITHOUT them, the first unauthenticated POST to /api/global/users/init owns the instance: packages/worker/src/api/index.ts:10-65 lists that route in PUBLIC_ENDPOINTS and worker/src/middleware/cloudRestricted.ts:10 waves it through completely when SELF_HOSTED is set. It is ONE-SHOT (controllers/global/users.ts:238-244 returns 403 once any global user exists), so the seat goes to whoever gets there first and there is no second chance. hosting/.env ships both variables EMPTY, so a copy-paste deploy is the unsafe case. Ask the user for the email, generate the password, set both, and hand them over at the end."
22	  - "AFTER THE FIRST ACCOUNT, REGISTRATION IS CLOSED BY DESIGN AND YOU DO NOT NEED A SETTING FOR IT. packages/worker/src/api/routes/global/users.ts:115-127,139 puts user creation and invitation on adminRoutes, and joining requires an invite code. So unlike most of this library there is no open sign-up page to close. ⚠️ Do not read that as 'nothing is exposed': see the CouchDB quirk below for what an anonymous request CAN reach."
23	  - "⛔⛔ THE PROXY EXPOSES COUCHDB ON THE PUBLIC URL AT /db/, SO COUCH_DB_PASSWORD IS AN INTERNET-FACING CREDENTIAL. hosting/proxy/nginx.prod.conf:236-239 is location /db/ proxying straight at couchdb-service with no auth layer of its own, and the / catch-all at :250-262 proxies MinIO. hosting/.env ships the CouchDB user and password, the MinIO keys, JWT_SECRET, API_ENCRYPTION_KEY and INTERNAL_API_KEY at the same placeholder values that appear in every Budibase tutorial. Leaving any of them means handing a stranger the entire database over HTTPS. GENERATE ALL SEVEN, long and alphanumeric, before you deploy. This is the single fastest way to lose a Budibase instance and it does not look like a misconfiguration from the UI."
24	  - "⛔ SET API_ENCRYPTION_KEY AND JWT_SECRET EXPLICITLY, AND REUSE THE SAME VALUES ON EVERY REDEPLOY. API_ENCRYPTION_KEY encrypts values at rest; packages/worker/src/api/controllers/global/self.ts:31-35 encrypts every issued Budibase API key with it, so changing it silently invalidates them all. packages/backend-core/src/environment.ts:53-55 shows API_ENCRYPTION_KEY falling back to JWT_SECRET when unset, which means a deploy that sets only one of them still works and then breaks in a confusing way if the other is introduced later. Set both, record both in the handover, and never regenerate them casually. JWT_SECRET also signs sessions: change it and everyone is logged out."
25	  - "SET PLATFORM_URL ON BOTH app-service AND worker-service TO THE FULL PUBLIC https URL. packages/backend-core/src/configs/configs.ts:146-168 defaults it to http://localhost:10000 and lets the settings document override it in self-host. Left alone, invitation and password-reset emails carry localhost links, which is discovered by the first colleague you invite rather than by you. Generate the dname yourself in the full budibase-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud form so this is known at deploy time; a bare label gets a random suffix appended and will not match."
26	  - "PORT 10000, THROUGH THEIR OWN NGINX, AND NOTHING ELSE. proxy-service publishes ${MAIN_PORT}:10000 and hosting/proxy/nginx.prod.conf:63 listens on 10000 inside the container. Set MAIN_PORT=10000, publish 10000, and pass port 10000 to deploy_compose. Do NOT publish app-service 4002, worker-service 4003, MinIO 9000 or CouchDB 5984 on the host: the builder calls paths that only exist through their proxy, and every one of those is a direct route into the data. Health probe: GET /health, which returns 200 with a JSON status body from nginx itself."
27	  - "FORCE compose_engine docker. proxy-service sets RESOLVER=[ip], which is Docker's embedded DNS, and nginx.prod.conf:26 uses it in a resolver directive to look the upstreams up at request time. Under podman that address does not resolve, so the proxy answers 502 for everything while every container looks healthy, which is the worst kind of failure to debug."
28	  - "PERSIST THREE NAMED VOLUMES AND DO NOT SHORTEN THE LIST: couchdb3_data on /data (apps, tables, users, settings AND the Lucene index), minio_data on /data (uploads, attachments, built app bundles) and redis_data on /data (sessions and the automation queue). Use NAMED volumes, never a bind mount under the project directory, because a source re-upload replaces the project directory. Losing couchdb3_data loses the apps; losing minio_data leaves apps that reference files which no longer exist, which is the more confusing of the two."
29	  - "SIZE FOR MEMORY, AND THE DISK IS PART OF THE POINT HERE. m1.large (4 vCPU / 8 GB, 80 GB disk) at GBP 0.0486/hr. Reasoning, not measurement: hosting/couchdb/clouseau/clouseau:3 starts the Lucene indexer with -Xmx2G on its own, and beside it run two Node services, MinIO, Redis and nginx, so m1.medium's 4 GB is not credible. m1.mem16 would give double the RAM for GBP 0.007/hr more but HALF the disk (40 GB), and since this is the entry where the database AND the uploads both live on the VM's disk, the 80 GB is the reason to prefer m1.large. m1.large is ABOVE the no-card trial ceiling of m1.medium, so a trial user cannot deploy this: say so BEFORE the plan is approved, not after a quota rejection. Measure real usage on your run and write the number back."
30	  - "⛔ TELL THE USER ABOUT THE ONE-APP LIMIT BEFORE THEY PAY FOR A VM. packages/pro/src/constants/licenses.ts SELF_FREE_LICENSE, the licence in force when none is present, grants features [] and apps 1, with users, creators and rows UNLIMITED, userGroups 0 and appBackupRetentionDays 0. So an unlicensed self-hosted Budibase is one workspace with unlimited users and rows in it. That is a genuinely useful product and it is NOT what someone expects if they assumed self-hosting means everything unlocked. Say it in the plan, not afterwards."
31	  - "TELEMETRY IS ON IN THE SHIPPED COMPOSE. app-service sets ENABLE_ANALYTICS true. packages/backend-core/src/configs/configs.ts:173-205 shows self-host preferring the instance's own settings document and falling back to that variable, so it can be turned off in Organisation settings after boot, or simply not set at deploy time. Mention it; do not decide it silently for the user."
32	  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. Budibase creates and migrates its own CouchDB databases at boot. The first boot is slower than a single-container entry: six images to pull, one of which carries CouchDB plus a JVM, and the app container only creates the admin user after its routes are up."
33	  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan, the cost (about GBP 0.0486/hr, roughly GBP 35 a month, NOT inside the no-card trial), the one-app licence limit and the fact that the data lives on the app VM -> WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '4' (m1.large), NO managed database, port 10000."
34	  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built. Assemble the trimmed compose and its .env locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo. Pointing deploy_compose at the Budibase monorepo would make redu try to build a very large workspace that publishes its own images anyway."
35	  - "LICENCE: the root LICENSE file is a guidelines document rather than a licence. It states you can consider Budibase to be GPLv3 overall, with packages/pro under BSL and the packages that ship inside a built app under MPL 2.0. The BSL condition is about removing licence checks to bypass paid restrictions; running the official unmodified images in your own account is not that. Apps you BUILD with Budibase do not package GPLv3 code, which the same file says explicitly."
36	  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. The admin password, JWT_SECRET, API_ENCRYPTION_KEY, the CouchDB password and the MinIO keys all belong to the user. Hand them over in the session; the deploy log records that the placeholders were replaced and that an admin exists, never the values."
37	  - "AFTERWARDS: pass THIS file to get_deployment as redu_md and write the merged redu_md_markdown back. ⚠️ That merge refreshes last_deploy and appends one deploy-log line, and it does NOT write new quirks, so anything your run teaches has to be added by hand. The most useful additions here are the measured memory and disk figures, because upstream publishes neither for the compose stack."
38	  - "DELETING IT DELETES THE DATA, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF EVERY OTHER ENTRY IN THIS LIBRARY. There is no managed database left behind, so delete_deployment removes the app VM and the apps with it. Export anything worth keeping from the builder first, and say that out loud before running it."
39	---
40	
41	# Self-host Budibase on redu
42	
43	An internal-tools and admin-panel builder on infrastructure you own: Budibase's own production
44	stack, trimmed, on one VM, with a public HTTPS URL and an administrator account that exists before
45	anyone else can reach it.
46	
47	## What this deploys

116	  [ "$code" = "502" ] && echo "  502 is redu's proxy while the containers start. Wait and re-run." >&2

repo: https://github.com/Budibase/budibase
plan:

  - "⛔⛔ READ THIS BEFORE SIZING OR PROMISING ANYTHING: THERE IS NO MANAGED DATABASE IN THIS RECIPE, AND THAT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Budibase keeps every app definition, every internal table row, every user and every setting in COUCHDB, and redu has no managed CouchDB. Its files, attachments and built app bundles live in MINIO, and redu has no managed object store either. Both therefore run as containers on the app VM, on named volumes. Consequence, and say it to the user in these words BEFORE they approve: this is the entry in the library whose data does NOT survive the VM. A source re-upload keeps named volumes; delete_deployment, or losing the VM, takes the apps with it. Budibase's own workspace export and a scheduled couchdb dump are the backup story, not the platform."
  - "⛔ WHAT REDU CAN AND CANNOT REPLACE, SO NOBODY RE-DERIVES IT. CouchDB: NOT replaceable, no managed equivalent, and charts/budibase/values.yaml:883-890 says upstream does not support any other CouchDB image anyway. MinIO: NOT replaceable here, though values.yaml:806-826 shows it can point at an external S3-compatible bucket if the user brings one. Redis: replaceable with a redu managed Redis at +GBP 0.0174/hr, and NOT worth it by default, because it holds sessions, caches and the automation queue rather than a system of record; losing it costs a re-login. LiteLLM's Postgres: replaceable, but this recipe deletes LiteLLM entirely, see the next quirk, so there is nothing left to point at a managed database."
  - "DELETE litellm-service AND litellm-db. Two independent pieces of upstream evidence say the AI gateway is optional: charts/budibase/values.yaml:725-727 ships services.litellm.enabled FALSE by default, and packages/server/src/startup/index.ts:48-52 skips the LiteLLM readiness wait entirely when LITELLM_MASTER_KEY is unset. A third says it would be useless anyway on an unlicensed self-host: packages/pro/src/constants/licenses.ts gives SELF_FREE_LICENSE customAIConfigurations 0 and budibaseAICredits 0. So remove both services, remove them from every depends_on, and do NOT set LITELLM_MASTER_KEY or LITELLM_URL. ⚠️ If you set LITELLM_MASTER_KEY with no LiteLLM running, the app container blocks about 30 seconds at boot waiting for a readiness check that cannot succeed, then carries on: a slow boot that looks like a hang. Keeping LiteLLM also means a postgres:16 container on the app VM or a managed Postgres at +GBP 0.0174/hr, which changes the quote, so it is the user's call and not yours."
  - "⛔ PIN EVERY IMAGE. THE UPSTREAM COMPOSE PINS ONLY TWO OF EIGHT. budibase/apps, budibase/worker, budibase/proxy, minio/minio and redis are all written with no tag, which is :latest, on a file people copy verbatim. Registry-checked pins on 2026-08-17: budibase/apps:3.41.3, budibase/worker:3.41.3, budibase/proxy:3.41.3 (all published 2026-08-04, matching the newest GitHub release), budibase/database:2.1.0 (its newest, from 2026-03-13), minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z (the newest community MinIO tag, and it is from 2025), redis:7.4.10.   - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR, AND WHEN. SET BB_ADMIN_USER_EMAIL AND [REDACTED:value] IN THE ENV BEFORE THE FIRST BOOT, AND THIS IS THE ONE THING YOU MUST NOT SKIP. With them set, packages/server/src/startup/index.ts:199-238 creates the admin account inside the app container's startup, before redu's hostname is even routing, which is the safe-by-construction case. WITHOUT them, the first unauthenticated POST to /api/global/users/init owns the instance: packages/worker/src/api/index.ts:10-65 lists that route in PUBLIC_ENDPOINTS and worker/src/middleware/cloudRestricted.ts:10 waves it through completely when SELF_HOSTED is set.   - "AFTER THE FIRST ACCOUNT, REGISTRATION IS CLOSED BY DESIGN AND YOU DO NOT NEED A SETTING FOR IT. packages/worker/src/api/routes/global/users.ts:115-127,139 puts user creation and invitation on adminRoutes, and joining requires an invite code.   - "⛔⛔ THE PROXY EXPOSES COUCHDB ON THE PUBLIC URL AT /db/, SO COUCH_DB_PASSWORD IS AN INTERNET-FACING CREDENTIAL. hosting/proxy/nginx.prod.conf:236-239 is location /db/ proxying straight at couchdb-service with no auth layer of its own, and the / catch-all at :250-262 proxies MinIO. hosting/.env ships the CouchDB user and password, the MinIO keys, JWT_SECRET, API_ENCRYPTION_KEY and INTERNAL_API_KEY at the same placeholder values that appear in every Budibase tutorial. This is the single fastest way to lose a Budibase instance and it does not look like a misconfiguration from the UI."
  - "⛔ SET API_ENCRYPTION_KEY AND JWT_SECRET EXPLICITLY, AND REUSE THE SAME VALUES ON EVERY REDEPLOY.   - "SET PLATFORM_URL ON BOTH app-service AND worker-service TO THE FULL PUBLIC https URL. packages/backend-core/src/configs/configs.ts:146-168 defaults it to http://localhost:10000 and lets the settings document override it in self-host. Generate the dname yourself in the full budibase-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud form so this is known at deploy time; a bare label gets a random suffix appended and will not match."
  - "PORT 10000, THROUGH THEIR OWN NGINX, AND NOTHING ELSE. proxy-service publishes ${MAIN_PORT}:10000 and hosting/proxy/nginx.prod.conf:63 listens on 10000 inside the container. Set MAIN_PORT=10000, publish 10000, and pass port 10000 to deploy_compose. Do NOT publish app-service 4002, worker-service 4003, MinIO 9000 or CouchDB 5984 on the host: the builder calls paths that only exist through their proxy, and every one of those is a direct route into the data. Health probe: GET /health, which returns 200 with a JSON status body from nginx itself."
  - "FORCE compose_engine docker. proxy-service sets RESOLVER=[ip], which is Docker's embedded DNS, and nginx.prod.conf:26 uses it in a resolver directive to look the upstreams up at request time. Under podman that address does not resolve, so the proxy answers 502 for everything while every container looks healthy, which is the worst kind of failure to debug."
  - "PERSIST THREE NAMED VOLUMES AND DO NOT SHORTEN THE LIST: couchdb3_data on /data (apps, tables, users, settings AND the Lucene index), minio_data on /data (uploads, attachments, built app bundles) and redis_data on /data (sessions and the automation queue). Losing couchdb3_data loses the apps; losing minio_data leaves apps that reference files which no longer exist, which is the more confusing of the two."
  - "SIZE FOR MEMORY, AND THE DISK IS PART OF THE POINT HERE. m1.large (4 vCPU / 8 GB, 80 GB disk) at GBP 0.0486/hr. Measure real usage on your run and write the number back."
  - "⛔ TELL THE USER ABOUT THE ONE-APP LIMIT BEFORE THEY PAY FOR A VM. packages/pro/src/constants/licenses.ts SELF_FREE_LICENSE, the licence in force when none is present, grants features [] and apps 1, with users, creators and rows UNLIMITED, userGroups 0 and appBackupRetentionDays 0. So an unlicensed self-hosted Budibase is one workspace with unlimited users and rows in it. That is a genuinely useful product and it is NOT what someone expects if they assumed self-hosting means everything unlocked. Say it in the plan, not afterwards."
  - "TELEMETRY IS ON IN THE SHIPPED COMPOSE. app-service sets ENABLE_ANALYTICS true. packages/backend-core/src/configs/configs.ts:173-205 shows self-host preferring the instance's own settings document and falling back to that variable, so it can be turned off in Organisation settings after boot, or simply not set at deploy time.   - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. Budibase creates and migrates its own CouchDB databases at boot. The first boot is slower than a single-container entry: six images to pull, one of which carries CouchDB plus a JVM, and the app container only creates the admin user after its routes are up."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan, the cost (about GBP 0.0486/hr, roughly GBP 35 a month, NOT inside the no-card trial), the one-app licence limit and the fact that the data lives on the app VM -> WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '4' (m1.large), NO managed database, port 10000."

# Self-host Budibase on redu

An internal-tools and admin-panel builder on infrastructure you own: Budibase's own production
stack, trimmed, on one VM, with a public HTTPS URL and an administrator account that exists before
anyone else can reach it.

## What this deploys

- **Budibase** from its official pinned images: the app server, the worker, and their nginx proxy.
- **CouchDB and MinIO** alongside them, because they are Budibase's database and file store and
  there is no managed substitute for either.
- **Redis** for sessions and the automation queue.
- Named volumes for all three, and a public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.0486/hour, roughly GBP 35 a month. **Above the no-card trial ceiling**, so this one
needs a payment method.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Budibase on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## Two things to know before you approve the plan

**Your data lives on the app VM.** Every other entry in this library puts your data in a managed
database on its own machine, which survives the app being redeployed or deleted. Budibase stores
apps, tables, users and settings in CouchDB and your files in MinIO, and redu offers neither as a
managed service, so both run beside the app on named volumes. Deleting the deployment deletes the
data with it. Export from the builder before you tear anything down.

**Unlicensed self-hosting is one workspace.** The licence Budibase uses when none is present grants
unlimited users, unlimited creators and unlimited rows, and exactly **one app**. That is a real
product and it is not what "self-hosted means everything unlocked" sounds like, so it is here rather
than in a footnote.

## The three that actually break it

**The admin account.** Set `BB_ADMIN_USER_EMAIL` and `[REDACTED:value]` before the first
boot and the account is created inside the container, before the hostname routes. Leave them empty,
as the shipped environment file does, and one unauthenticated POST claims the instance. It is
one-shot, so there is no second chance.

**The CouchDB password.** Budibase's proxy serves CouchDB at `/db/` on the same public URL as the
app. The shipped environment file uses a placeholder value that every tutorial reproduces. Generate
it, along with the MinIO keys, `JWT_SECRET` and `API_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.

**The unpinned images.** Five of the eight images in the upstream compose have no tag at all, which
means `:latest`. Pin them, and keep the three Budibase images on the same version as each other.

## Prove the admin seat is taken

Run this once the deploy reports ready. It checks the thing that matters rather than the flag that
describes it: Budibase caches its own "an admin exists" answer for an hour by default, so the flag
can be stale in exactly the situation you care about.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove nobody else can claim your Budibase, and claim it if the seat is still open.
#   BB_ADMIN_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value] ./verify-admin.sh budibase-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud you@example.com
# Exit 0 = the seat was already taken. 1 = it was OPEN and this script has just claimed it.
#      2 = inconclusive, it may still be starting: re-run, and do NOT read it as a pass.
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-admin.sh <host> <admin-email>}"
EMAIL="${2:?usage: verify-admin.sh <host> <admin-email>}"
: "${BB_ADMIN_PASSWORD:«REDACTED:assigned:52ed1607» BB_ADMIN_PASSWORD first; do not pass it as an argument}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# 1. GATE. Every assertion below is vacuous unless Budibase itself is answering.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/chk" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/global/configs/checklist")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: the checklist answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2
  [ "$code" = "502" ] && echo "  502 is redu's proxy while the containers start. Wait and re-run." >&2
  exit 2
fi
if ! grep -q '"adminUser"' "$TMP/chk"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 200, but the body is not Budibase's checklist." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "gate OK: Budibase's worker is answering on this hostname."

# 2. The flag, as a HINT only: configs.ts caches it for CHECKLIST_CACHE_TTL, 3600s by default.
case "$(tr -d ' ' < "$TMP/chk")" in
  *'"adminUser":{"checked":true'*) echo "hint: the checklist says an admin exists (may be up to 1h stale)." ;;
  *) echo "hint: the checklist does NOT say an admin exists (may be up to 1h stale)." ;;
esac

# 3. The BEHAVIOUR, which is the only thing that settles it. This route is public in self-host
#    builds and one-shot: 403 means the seat is taken, 200 means it was there for the taking and
#    this script has just taken it. Body on stdin so it never appears in ps.
code=$(printf '{"email":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]","tenantId":"default"}' "$EMAIL" "$BB_ADMIN_PASSWORD" \
  | curl -sS -o "$TMP/init" -w '%{http_code}' -H 'content-type: application/json' \
         --data-binary @- "https://$HOST/api/global/users/init")
case "$code" in
  403) echo "OK: /api/global/users/init refused with 403, so the admin seat is already claimed." ;;
  200|201)
    echo "WARNING: the seat was OPEN. This script has just claimed it for $EMAIL." >&2
    echo "  It was claimable by anyone who found the URL until now. Sign in and check the user" >&2
    echo "  list for accounts you did not create before you trust this instance." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
  404)
    echo "FAIL: that route answered 404, so it has moved and this check proves NOTHING." >&2
    echo "  Do not leave the instance running on a public hostname until you have re-verified." >&2
    exit 2 ;;
  *) echo "INCONCLUSIVE: unexpected HTTP $code from the init route." >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

# 4. Prove the account actually signs in. Note the field is username, not email, and the tenant
#    segment is required: for a single-tenant self-host it is "default".
code=$(printf '{"username":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' "$EMAIL" "$BB_ADMIN_PASSWORD" \
  | curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H 'content-type: application/json' \
         --data-binary @- "https://$HOST/api/global/auth/default/login")
if [ "$code" = "200" ]; then
  echo "OK: the admin account signs in."
else
  echo "WARNING: the seat is claimed but this password did not sign in (HTTP $code)." >&2
  echo "  Somebody else may hold the account, or the password differs. Investigate now." >&2
  exit 1
fi
```

## Deploy log

- Not yet deployed. The flavor and the hourly rate on this page are reasoning from Budibase's own
  compose, chart and licence source, not a measurement. The first real run should record the
  container memory, the disk used by CouchDB and MinIO after a workspace exists, and how long the
  six images take to pull.

file.content:
# optional ports are specified throughout for more advanced use cases.

services:
  app-service:
    restart: unless-stopped
    image: budibase/apps
    container_name: bbapps
    environment:
      SELF_HOSTED: 1
      COUCH_DB_URL: http://${COUCH_DB_USER}:[REDACTED:conn-password]@couchdb-service:5984
      WORKER_URL: http://worker-service:4003
      MINIO_URL: http://minio-service:9000
      MINIO_ACCESS_KEY: [REDACTED:value]}
      MINIO_SECRET_KEY: [REDACTED:value]}
      INTERNAL_API_KEY: [REDACTED:value]}
      BUDIBASE_ENVIRONMENT: ${BUDIBASE_ENVIRONMENT}
      PORT: 4002
      API_ENCRYPTION_KEY: [REDACTED:value]}
      JWT_SECRET: [REDACTED:value]}
      LOG_LEVEL: info
      ENABLE_ANALYTICS: "true"
      REDIS_URL: redis-service:6379
      REDIS_PASSWORD: [REDACTED:value]}
      REDIS_USERNAME: ${REDIS_USERNAME:-}
      LITELLM_URL: http://litellm-service:4000
      LITELLM_MASTER_KEY: ${LITELLM_MASTER_KEY}
      BB_ADMIN_USER_EMAIL: ${BB_ADMIN_USER_EMAIL}
      [REDACTED:value]: [REDACTED:value]}
      PLUGINS_DIR: ${PLUGINS_DIR}
      OFFLINE_MODE: ${OFFLINE_MODE:-}
    depends_on:
      - worker-service
      - redis-service
      - litellm-service
  #    volumes:
  #      - /some/path/to/plugins:/plugins

  worker-service:
    restart: unless-stopped
    image: budibase/worker
    container_name: bbworker
    environment:
      SELF_HOSTED: 1
      PORT: 4003
      CLUSTER_PORT: ${MAIN_PORT}
      API_ENCRYPTION_KEY: [REDACTED:value]}
      JWT_SECRET: [REDACTED:value]}
      MINIO_ACCESS_KEY: [REDACTED:value]}
      MINIO_SECRET_KEY: [REDACTED:value]}
      MINIO_URL: http://minio-service:9000
      APPS_URL: http://app-service:4002
      COUCH_DB_USERNAME: ${COUCH_DB_USER}
      COUCH_DB_PASSWORD: [REDACTED:value]}
      COUCH_DB_URL: http://${COUCH_DB_USER}:[REDACTED:conn-password]@couchdb-service:5984
      INTERNAL_API_KEY: [REDACTED:value]}
      REDIS_URL: redis-service:6379
      REDIS_PASSWORD: [REDACTED:value]}
      REDIS_USERNAME: ${REDIS_USERNAME:-}
      LITELLM_URL: http://litellm-service:4000
      LITELLM_MASTER_KEY: ${LITELLM_MASTER_KEY}
      OFFLINE_MODE: ${OFFLINE_MODE:-}
    depends_on:
      - redis-service
      - minio-service
      - litellm-service

  minio-service:
    restart: unless-stopped
    image: minio/minio
    volumes:
      - minio_data:/data
    environment:
      MINIO_ACCESS_KEY: [REDACTED:value]}
      MINIO_SECRET_KEY: [REDACTED:value]}
      MINIO_BROWSER: "off"
    command: server /data --console-address ":9001"
    healthcheck:
      test: "timeout 5s bash -c ':> /dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/9000' || exit 1"
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 20s
      retries: 3

  proxy-service:
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${MAIN_PORT}:10000"
    container_name: bbproxy
    image: budibase/proxy
    environment:
      - PROXY_RATE_LIMIT_WEBHOOKS_PER_SECOND=10
      - PROXY_RATE_LIMIT_API_PER_SECOND=50
      - APPS_UPSTREAM_URL=http://app-service:4002
      - WORKER_UPSTREAM_URL=http://worker-service:4003
      - MINIO_UPSTREAM_URL=http://minio-service:9000
      - COUCHDB_UPSTREAM_URL=http://couchdb-service:5984
      - RESOLVER=[ip]
    depends_on:
      - minio-service
      - worker-service
      - app-service
      - couchdb-service

  couchdb-service:
    restart: unless-stopped
    image: budibase/database:2.1.0
    environment:
      - COUCHDB_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value]}
      - COUCHDB_USER=${COUCH_DB_USER}
      - TARGETBUILD=docker-compose
      - DATA_DIR=/data
    volumes:
      - couchdb3_data:/data

  redis-service:
    restart: unless-stopped
    image: redis
    command: redis-server --requirepass "${REDIS_PASSWORD}"
    volumes:
      - redis_data:/data

  litellm-service:
    restart: unless-stopped
    image: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-v1.83.10-stable
    ports:
      - "${LITELLM_PORT:-4000}:4000"
    volumes:
      - ./litellm_config.yaml:/app/config.yaml
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: "postgresql://${LITELLM_DB_USER}:[REDACTED:conn-password]@litellm-db:5432/${LITELLM_DB_NAME}"
      STORE_MODEL_IN_DB: "True"
      LITELLM_REASONING_AUTO_SUMMARY: "true"
      LITELLM_MASTER_KEY: ${LITELLM_MASTER_KEY}
      LITELLM_SALT_KEY: [REDACTED:value]}
    command: ["--config", "/app/config.yaml"]
    depends_on:
      - litellm-db
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget --no-verbose --tries=1 http://localhost:4000/health/liveliness || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 40s

  litellm-db:
    restart: unless-stopped
    image: postgres:16
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: ${LITELLM_DB_NAME}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${LITELLM_DB_USER}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: [REDACTED:value]}
    volumes:
      - litellm_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -d ${LITELLM_DB_NAME} -U ${LITELLM_DB_USER}"]
      interval: 1s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10

volumes:
  couchdb3_data:
    driver: local
  minio_data:
    driver: local
  redis_data:
    driver: local
  litellm_data:
    driver: local

---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/Budibase/budibase
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: budibase/apps:3.41.3 (plus worker, proxy, database, minio, redis)
  port: 10000
  vm: m1.large
  flavor_id: "4"
  database: none. Budibase's system of record is CouchDB, which redu does not offer managed, so it runs on the app VM on a named volume
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0486
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: budibase
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ READ THIS BEFORE SIZING OR PROMISING ANYTHING: THERE IS NO MANAGED DATABASE IN THIS RECIPE, AND THAT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Budibase keeps every app definition, every internal table row, every user and every setting in COUCHDB, and redu has no managed CouchDB. Its files, attachments and built app bundles live in MINIO, and redu has no managed object store either. Both therefore run as containers on the app VM, on named volumes. Consequence, and say it to the user in these words BEFORE they approve: this is the entry in the library whose data does NOT survive the VM. A source re-upload keeps named volumes; delete_deployment, or losing the VM, takes the apps with it. Budibase's own workspace export and a scheduled couchdb dump are the backup story, not the platform."
  - "⛔ WHAT REDU CAN AND CANNOT REPLACE, SO NOBODY RE-DERIVES IT. CouchDB: NOT replaceable, no managed equivalent, and charts/budibase/values.yaml:883-890 says upstream does not support any other CouchDB image anyway. MinIO: NOT replaceable here, though values.yaml:806-826 shows it can point at an external S3-compatible bucket if the user brings one. Redis: replaceable with a redu managed Redis at +GBP 0.0174/hr, and NOT worth it by default, because it holds sessions, caches and the automation queue rather than a system of record; losing it costs a re-login. LiteLLM's Postgres: replaceable, but this recipe deletes LiteLLM entirely, see the next quirk, so there is nothing left to point at a managed database."
  - "DELETE litellm-service AND litellm-db. Two independent pieces of upstream evidence say the AI gateway is optional: charts/budibase/values.yaml:725-727 ships services.litellm.enabled FALSE by default, and packages/server/src/startup/index.ts:48-52 skips the LiteLLM readiness wait entirely when LITELLM_MASTER_KEY is unset. A third says it would be useless anyway on an unlicensed self-host: packages/pro/src/constants/licenses.ts gives SELF_FREE_LICENSE customAIConfigurations 0 and budibaseAICredits 0. So remove both services, remove them from every depends_on, and do NOT set LITELLM_MASTER_KEY or LITELLM_URL. ⚠️ If you set LITELLM_MASTER_KEY with no LiteLLM running, the app container blocks about 30 seconds at boot waiting for a readiness check that cannot succeed, then carries on: a slow boot that looks like a hang. Keeping LiteLLM also means a postgres:16 container on the app VM or a managed Postgres at +GBP 0.0174/hr, which changes the quote, so it is the user's call and not yours."
  - "⛔ PIN EVERY IMAGE. THE UPSTREAM COMPOSE PINS ONLY TWO OF EIGHT. budibase/apps, budibase/worker, budibase/proxy, minio/minio and redis are all written with no tag, which is :latest, on a file people copy verbatim. Registry-checked pins on 2026-08-17: budibase/apps:3.41.3, budibase/worker:3.41.3, budibase/proxy:3.41.3 (all published 2026-08-04, matching the newest GitHub release), budibase/database:2.1.0 (its newest, from 2026-03-13), minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z (the newest community MinIO tag, and it is from 2025), redis:7.4.10. Keep the three Budibase images on the SAME version as each other. ⚠️ Ignore the v3.42.0-cloud tags: they are the hosted build, they have no matching GitHub release, and they are not what self-hosting docs describe."
  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR, AND WHEN. SET BB_ADMIN_USER_EMAIL AND [REDACTED:value] IN THE ENV BEFORE THE FIRST BOOT, AND THIS IS THE ONE THING YOU MUST NOT SKIP. With them set, packages/server/src/startup/index.ts:199-238 creates the admin account inside the app container's startup, before redu's hostname is even routing, which is the safe-by-construction case. WITHOUT them, the first unauthenticated POST to /api/global/users/init owns the instance: packages/worker/src/api/index.ts:10-65 lists that route in PUBLIC_ENDPOINTS and worker/src/middleware/cloudRestricted.ts:10 waves it through completely when SELF_HOSTED is set. It is ONE-SHOT (controllers/global/users.ts:238-244 returns 403 once any global user exists), so the seat goes to whoever gets there first and there is no second chance. hosting/.env ships both variables EMPTY, so a copy-paste deploy is the unsafe case. Ask the user for the email, generate the password, set both, and hand them over at the end."
  - "AFTER THE FIRST ACCOUNT, REGISTRATION IS CLOSED BY DESIGN AND YOU DO NOT NEED A SETTING FOR IT. packages/worker/src/api/routes/global/users.ts:115-127,139 puts user creation and invitation on adminRoutes, and joining requires an invite code. So unlike most of this library there is no open sign-up page to close. ⚠️ Do not read that as 'nothing is exposed': see the CouchDB quirk below for what an anonymous request CAN reach."
  - "⛔⛔ THE PROXY EXPOSES COUCHDB ON THE PUBLIC URL AT /db/, SO COUCH_DB_PASSWORD IS AN INTERNET-FACING CREDENTIAL. hosting/proxy/nginx.prod.conf:236-239 is location /db/ proxying straight at couchdb-service with no auth layer of its own, and the / catch-all at :250-262 proxies MinIO. hosting/.env ships the CouchDB user and password, the MinIO keys, JWT_SECRET, API_ENCRYPTION_KEY and INTERNAL_API_KEY at the same placeholder values that appear in every Budibase tutorial. Leaving any of them means handing a stranger the entire database over HTTPS. GENERATE ALL SEVEN, long and alphanumeric, before you deploy. This is the single fastest way to lose a Budibase instance and it does not look like a misconfiguration from the UI."
  - "⛔ SET API_ENCRYPTION_KEY AND JWT_SECRET EXPLICITLY, AND REUSE THE SAME VALUES ON EVERY REDEPLOY. API_ENCRYPTION_KEY encrypts values at rest; packages/worker/src/api/controllers/global/self.ts:31-35 encrypts every issued Budibase API key with it, so changing it silently invalidates them all. packages/backend-core/src/environment.ts:53-55 shows API_ENCRYPTION_KEY falling back to JWT_SECRET when unset, which means a deploy that sets only one of them still works and then breaks in a confusing way if the other is introduced later. Set both, record both in the handover, and never regenerate them casually. JWT_SECRET also signs sessions: change it and everyone is logged out."
  - "SET PLATFORM_URL ON BOTH app-service AND worker-service TO THE FULL PUBLIC https URL. packages/backend-core/src/configs/configs.ts:146-168 defaults it to http://localhost:10000 and lets the settings document override it in self-host. Left alone, invitation and password-reset emails carry localhost links, which is discovered by the first colleague you invite rather than by you. Generate the dname yourself in the full budibase-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud form so this is known at deploy time; a bare label gets a random suffix appended and will not match."
  - "PORT 10000, THROUGH THEIR OWN NGINX, AND NOTHING ELSE. proxy-service publishes ${MAIN_PORT}:10000 and hosting/proxy/nginx.prod.conf:63 listens on 10000 inside the container. Set MAIN_PORT=10000, publish 10000, and pass port 10000 to deploy_compose. Do NOT publish app-service 4002, worker-service 4003, MinIO 9000 or CouchDB 5984 on the host: the builder calls paths that only exist through their proxy, and every one of those is a direct route into the data. Health probe: GET /health, which returns 200 with a JSON status body from nginx itself."
  - "FORCE compose_engine docker. proxy-service sets RESOLVER=[ip], which is Docker's embedded DNS, and nginx.prod.conf:26 uses it in a resolver directive to look the upstreams up at request time. Under podman that address does not resolve, so the proxy answers 502 for everything while every container looks healthy, which is the worst kind of failure to debug."
  - "PERSIST THREE NAMED VOLUMES AND DO NOT SHORTEN THE LIST: couchdb3_data on /data (apps, tables, users, settings AND the Lucene index), minio_data on /data (uploads, attachments, built app bundles) and redis_data on /data (sessions and the automation queue). Use NAMED volumes, never a bind mount under the project directory, because a source re-upload replaces the project directory. Losing couchdb3_data loses the apps; losing minio_data leaves apps that reference files which no longer exist, which is the more confusing of the two."
  - "SIZE FOR MEMORY, AND THE DISK IS PART OF THE POINT HERE. m1.large (4 vCPU / 8 GB, 80 GB disk) at GBP 0.0486/hr. Reasoning, not measurement: hosting/couchdb/clouseau/clouseau:3 starts the Lucene indexer with -Xmx2G on its own, and beside it run two Node services, MinIO, Redis and nginx, so m1.medium's 4 GB is not credible. m1.mem16 would give double the RAM for GBP 0.007/hr more but HALF the disk (40 GB), and since this is the entry where the database AND the uploads both live on the VM's disk, the 80 GB is the reason to prefer m1.large. m1.large is ABOVE the no-card trial ceiling of m1.medium, so a trial user cannot deploy this: say so BEFORE the plan is approved, not after a quota rejection. Measure real usage on your run and write the number back."
  - "⛔ TELL THE USER ABOUT THE ONE-APP LIMIT BEFORE THEY PAY FOR A VM. packages/pro/src/constants/licenses.ts SELF_FREE_LICENSE, the licence in force when none is present, grants features [] and apps 1, with users, creators and rows UNLIMITED, userGroups 0 and appBackupRetentionDays 0. So an unlicensed self-hosted Budibase is one workspace with unlimited users and rows in it. That is a genuinely useful product and it is NOT what someone expects if they assumed self-hosting means everything unlocked. Say it in the plan, not afterwards."
  - "TELEMETRY IS ON IN THE SHIPPED COMPOSE. app-service sets ENABLE_ANALYTICS true. packages/backend-core/src/configs/configs.ts:173-205 shows self-host preferring the instance's own settings document and falling back to that variable, so it can be turned off in Organisation settings after boot, or simply not set at deploy time. Mention it; do not decide it silently for the user."
  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. Budibase creates and migrates its own CouchDB databases at boot. The first boot is slower than a single-container entry: six images to pull, one of which carries CouchDB plus a JVM, and the app container only creates the admin user after its routes are up."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan, the cost (about GBP 0.0486/hr, roughly GBP 35 a month, NOT inside the no-card trial), the one-app licence limit and the fact that the data lives on the app VM -> WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '4' (m1.large), NO managed database, port 10000."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built. Assemble the trimmed compose and its .env locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo. Pointing deploy_compose at the Budibase monorepo would make redu try to build a very large workspace that publishes its own images anyway."
  - "LICENCE: the root LICENSE file is a guidelines document rather than a licence. It states you can consider Budibase to be GPLv3 overall, with packages/pro under BSL and the packages that ship inside a built app under MPL 2.0. The BSL condition is about removing licence checks to bypass paid restrictions; running the official unmodified images in your own account is not that. Apps you BUILD with Budibase do not package GPLv3 code, which the same file says explicitly."
  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. The admin password, JWT_SECRET, API_ENCRYPTION_KEY, the CouchDB password and the MinIO keys all belong to the user. Hand them over in the session; the deploy log records that the placeholders were replaced and that an admin exists, never the values."
  - "AFTERWARDS: pass THIS file to get_deployment as redu_md and write the merged redu_md_markdown back. ⚠️ That merge refreshes last_deploy and appends one deploy-log line, and it does NOT write new quirks, so anything your run teaches has to be added by hand. The most useful additions here are the measured memory and disk figures, because upstream publishes neither for the compose stack."
  - "DELETING IT DELETES THE DATA, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF EVERY OTHER ENTRY IN THIS LIBRARY. There is no managed database left behind, so delete_deployment removes the app VM and the apps with it. Export anything worth keeping from the builder first, and say that out loud before running it."

# Self-host Budibase on redu

An internal-tools and admin-panel builder on infrastructure you own: Budibase's own production
stack, trimmed, on one VM, with a public HTTPS URL and an administrator account that exists before
anyone else can reach it.

## What this deploys

- **Budibase** from its official pinned images: the app server, the worker, and their nginx proxy.
- **CouchDB and MinIO** alongside them, because they are Budibase's database and file store and
  there is no managed substitute for either.
- **Redis** for sessions and the automation queue.
- Named volumes for all three, and a public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.0486/hour, roughly GBP 35 a month. **Above the no-card trial ceiling**, so this one
needs a payment method.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Budibase on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## Two things to know before you approve the plan

**Your data lives on the app VM.** Every other entry in this library puts your data in a managed
database on its own machine, which survives the app being redeployed or deleted. Budibase stores
apps, tables, users and settings in CouchDB and your files in MinIO, and redu offers neither as a
managed service, so both run beside the app on named volumes. Deleting the deployment deletes the
data with it. Export from the builder before you tear anything down.

**Unlicensed self-hosting is one workspace.** The licence Budibase uses when none is present grants
unlimited users, unlimited creators and unlimited rows, and exactly **one app**. That is a real
product and it is not what "self-hosted means everything unlocked" sounds like, so it is here rather
than in a footnote.

## The three that actually break it

**The admin account.** Set `BB_ADMIN_USER_EMAIL` and `[REDACTED:value]` before the first
boot and the account is created inside the container, before the hostname routes. Leave them empty,
as the shipped environment file does, and one unauthenticated POST claims the instance. It is
one-shot, so there is no second chance.

**The CouchDB password.** Budibase's proxy serves CouchDB at `/db/` on the same public URL as the
app. The shipped environment file uses a placeholder value that every tutorial reproduces. Generate
it, along with the MinIO keys, `JWT_SECRET` and `API_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.

**The unpinned images.** Five of the eight images in the upstream compose have no tag at all, which
means `:latest`. Pin them, and keep the three Budibase images on the same version as each other.

## Prove the admin seat is taken

Run this once the deploy reports ready. It checks the thing that matters rather than the flag that
describes it: Budibase caches its own "an admin exists" answer for an hour by default, so the flag
can be stale in exactly the situation you care about.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove nobody else can claim your Budibase, and claim it if the seat is still open.
#   BB_ADMIN_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value] ./verify-admin.sh budibase-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud you@example.com
# Exit 0 = the seat was already taken. 1 = it was OPEN and this script has just claimed it.
#      2 = inconclusive, it may still be starting: re-run, and do NOT read it as a pass.
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-admin.sh <host> <admin-email>}"
EMAIL="${2:?usage: verify-admin.sh <host> <admin-email>}"
: "${BB_ADMIN_PASSWORD:«REDACTED:assigned:52ed1607» BB_ADMIN_PASSWORD first; do not pass it as an argument}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# 1. GATE. Every assertion below is vacuous unless Budibase itself is answering.
code=$(curl -sSL -o "$TMP/chk" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/global/configs/checklist")
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: the checklist answered HTTP $code, not 200." >&2
  [ "$code" = "502" ] && echo "  502 is redu's proxy while the containers start. Wait and re-run." >&2
  exit 2
fi
if ! grep -q '"adminUser"' "$TMP/chk"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 200, but the body is not Budibase's checklist." >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "gate OK: Budibase's worker is answering on this hostname."

# 2. The flag, as a HINT only: configs.ts caches it for CHECKLIST_CACHE_TTL, 3600s by default.
case "$(tr -d ' ' < "$TMP/chk")" in
  *'"adminUser":{"checked":true'*) echo "hint: the checklist says an admin exists (may be up to 1h stale)." ;;
  *) echo "hint: the checklist does NOT say an admin exists (may be up to 1h stale)." ;;
esac

# 3. The BEHAVIOUR, which is the only thing that settles it. This route is public in self-host
#    builds and one-shot: 403 means the seat is taken, 200 means it was there for the taking and
#    this script has just taken it. Body on stdin so it never appears in ps.
code=$(printf '{"email":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]","tenantId":"default"}' "$EMAIL" "$BB_ADMIN_PASSWORD" \
  | curl -sS -o "$TMP/init" -w '%{http_code}' -H 'content-type: application/json' \
         --data-binary @- "https://$HOST/api/global/users/init")
case "$code" in
  403) echo "OK: /api/global/users/init refused with 403, so the admin seat is already claimed." ;;
  200|201)
    echo "WARNING: the seat was OPEN. This script has just claimed it for $EMAIL." >&2
    echo "  It was claimable by anyone who found the URL until now. Sign in and check the user" >&2
    echo "  list for accounts you did not create before you trust this instance." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
  404)
    echo "FAIL: that route answered 404, so it has moved and this check proves NOTHING." >&2

esac

# 4. Prove the account actually signs in. Note the field is username, not email, and the tenant
#    segment is required: for a single-tenant self-host it is "default".
code=$(printf '{"username":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' "$EMAIL" "$BB_ADMIN_PASSWORD" \
  | curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H 'content-type: application/json' \
         --data-binary @- "https://$HOST/api/global/auth/default/login")
if [ "$code" = "200" ]; then
  echo "OK: the admin account signs in."
else
  echo "WARNING: the seat is claimed but this password did not sign in (HTTP $code)." >&2
  echo "  Somebody else may hold the account, or the password differs. Investigate now." >&2
  exit 1
fi

A rebooted VM (or a rebuilt cluster member) comes back with nothing running, never rejoins the pool, and silently drains capacity. Measured at 50-60s outages before this was understood. - ⚠ This app is told its OWN url (BASE_URL / SITE_URL / callback / hostname env detected). Generate the dname UP FRONT and pass it as `dname`, wiring that exact value into the env - do not let redu auto-generate the URL. — 44 of 46 real deploys carrying env embedded their own redu.cloud URL. redu appends a random 8-char suffix to a bare name, so an auto-generated URL will NOT match anything you wired, and a redeploy changes it again - silently breaking OAuth callbacks and cookies. - • Does this app CREATE its schema on first boot? If not, pass migrate_command - otherwise it deploys, passes the probe, and 502s on real use. — #1: deploy-but-502 is the classic database-backed failure. Auto-migrating apps need nothing; the rest need one command. Asking is stack-independent; guessing the framework is not. - • This stack runs its OWN database container, so the data lives on the app VM. It is on a named volume, so it survives a container restart but NOT the VM. That is fine for a demo. For anything you would miss: pass database:'managed' (and db_engine) to get a separate managed DB VM with nightly backups, and have the compose read the injected DATABASE_URL/PG*/MYSQL_* env. Say which you chose and why. — State on the app VM has no automated backups, dies with the VM, and blocks upgrade_to_cluster, which refuses a stateful VM - so making the app highly available later needs a data migration first. - • ~12 services detected - size the VM up and expect a 10-20 min settle. — #22: heavy stacks legitimately take 10-20 min; SigNoz was also RAM-starved at a small flavor. - ✔ redu.md found — reusing its recorded plan and fixes. _Generated by redu plan_deploy. Confirm before provisioning._ --- ## How this run applies redu.md (decisions taken before deploy) - **Six services, not eight.** `litellm-service` and `litellm-db` are deleted, and removed from every `depends_on`. `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` / `LITELLM_URL` are left unset (setting the key with no LiteLLM running costs ~30s of blocked boot). - **Every image pinned:** `budibase/apps:3.41.3`, `budibase/worker:3.41.3`, `budibase/proxy:3.41.3`, `budibase/database:2.1.0`, `minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z`, `redis:7.4.10`. - **No managed database and no managed Redis.** CouchDB and MinIO have no managed equivalent on redu; Redis holds sessions and the automation queue, not a system of record, so paying +GBP 0.0174/hr for it is not worth it. All three run on the app VM on **named volumes** (`couchdb3_data`, `minio_data`, `redis_data`). - **`compose_engine: docker`**, forced. The proxy uses `RESOLVER=[ip]` (Docker's embedded DNS); under podman it 502s everything while all containers look healthy. - **Seven secrets generated** (JWT_SECRET, API_ENCRYPTION_KEY, INTERNAL_API_KEY, COUCH_DB_PASSWORD, MINIO_ACCESS_KEY, MINIO_SECRET_KEY, REDIS_PASSWORD) — the proxy serves CouchDB at `/db/` on the public URL, so these are internet-facing. - **Admin account created before the hostname routes**, via `BB_ADMIN_USER_EMAIL` / `[REDACTED:value]` set in the env at first boot. - **`dname` fixed up front** so `PLATFORM_URL` on app-service and worker-service matches the real URL. - **Port 10000 only.** Nothing else published on the host. - **No `migrate_command`.** Budibase creates and migrates its own CouchDB databases at boot. ## What you should know before approving - **GBP 0.0486/hr ≈ GBP 35/month.** Above the no-card trial ceiling (m1.medium), so this needs a payment method. - **Your data lives on the app VM.** Deleting the deployment deletes the apps, tables, users and uploads with it. I've read `redu.md`, fetched Budibase's upstream compose at 3.41.3, and written the plan to `redu-deploy-plan.md`. Here it is before anything is created:

## Plan

**One `m1.large` VM (4 vCPU / 8 GB / 80 GB disk) — GBP 0.0486/hr, ≈ GBP 35/month.** Six containers via `deploy_compose`, forced onto the **docker** engine (the Budibase proxy uses `RESOLVER=[ip]`, Docker's embedded DNS — under podman it 502s everything while every container looks healthy).

| | |
|---|---|
| Images, all pinned | `budibase/apps:3.41.3`, `budibase/worker:3.41.3`, `budibase/proxy:3.41.3`, `budibase/database:2.1.0`, `minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z`, `redis:7.4.10` |
| Removed | `litellm-service` + `litellm-db`, and every `depends_on` reference — off by default upstream, and useless on an unlicensed self-host |
| Managed services | **none** — no managed DB, no managed Redis |
| Volumes | `couchdb3_data`, `minio_data`, `redis_data` (named) |
| Exposed | port 10000 only, through Budibase's own nginx |

## Three things to know before you approve

**This is above the no-card trial ceiling.** The trial tops out at m1.medium; this needs a payment method on the account.

**Your data does not survive the VM.** Budibase keeps every app definition, every table row, every user and every setting in CouchDB, and its files and built app bundles in MinIO. redu offers neither as a managed service, so both run as containers on the app VM on named volumes. A source re-upload keeps them; `delete_deployment`, or losing the VM, takes the apps with it. Budibase's own workspace export and a scheduled CouchDB dump are the backup story here, not the platform. This is the one recipe in the library that works this way.

**Unlicensed self-hosting is one workspace.** The licence in force when none is present gives unlimited users, unlimited creators and unlimited rows — and exactly **one app**. Useful, but not "everything unlocked".

I'll generate all seven secrets (the proxy serves CouchDB at `/db/` on the public URL, so the CouchDB password is internet-facing) and create the admin account inside the container at first boot, before the hostname routes — otherwise the first unauthenticated POST to `/api/global/users/init` claims the instance, one-shot, no second chance.

# Budibase self-hosted on redu.cloud — trimmed from hosting/docker-compose.yaml at 3.41.3.
#
# Differences from upstream, all deliberate:
#   - litellm-service and litellm-db removed, and removed from every depends_on. The AI gateway is
#     disabled by default in the Helm chart and is inert on an unlicensed self-host. LITELLM_URL and
#     LITELLM_MASTER_KEY are left UNSET: setting the key with no LiteLLM running blocks the app
#     container ~30s at boot on a readiness check that cannot succeed.
#   - Every image pinned. Upstream tags only two of eight; the rest are :latest.
#   - PLATFORM_URL set on app-service and worker-service, so invite and password-reset emails carry
#     the real public URL instead of http://localhost:10000.
#   - ENABLE_ANALYTICS not set (telemetry off). Can be turned on later in Organisation settings.
#   - MAIN_PORT inlined as 10000. Only proxy-service publishes a host port.
#
# Secrets come from the project .env, which redu writes from deploy_compose's env argument.

services:
  app-service:
    restart: unless-stopped
    image: budibase/apps:3.41.3
    container_name: bbapps
    environment:
      SELF_HOSTED: 1
      COUCH_DB_URL: http://${COUCH_DB_USER}:[REDACTED:conn-password]@couchdb-service:5984
      WORKER_URL: http://worker-service:4003
      MINIO_URL: http://minio-service:9000
      MINIO_ACCESS_KEY: [REDACTED:value]}
      MINIO_SECRET_KEY: [REDACTED:value]}
      INTERNAL_API_KEY: [REDACTED:value]}
      BUDIBASE_ENVIRONMENT: PRODUCTION
      PORT: 4002
      API_ENCRYPTION_KEY: [REDACTED:value]}
      JWT_SECRET: [REDACTED:value]}
      LOG_LEVEL: info
      PLATFORM_URL: ${PLATFORM_URL}
      REDIS_URL: redis-service:6379
      REDIS_PASSWORD: [REDACTED:value]}
      BB_ADMIN_USER_EMAIL: ${BB_ADMIN_USER_EMAIL}
      [REDACTED:value]: [REDACTED:value]}
    depends_on:
      - worker-service
      - redis-service

  worker-service:
    restart: unless-stopped
    image: budibase/worker:3.41.3
    container_name: bbworker
    environment:
      SELF_HOSTED: 1
      PORT: 4003
      CLUSTER_PORT: 10000
      API_ENCRYPTION_KEY: [REDACTED:value]}
      JWT_SECRET: [REDACTED:value]}
      MINIO_ACCESS_KEY: [REDACTED:value]}
      MINIO_SECRET_KEY: [REDACTED:value]}
      MINIO_URL: http://minio-service:9000
      APPS_URL: http://app-service:4002
      COUCH_DB_USERNAME: ${COUCH_DB_USER}
      COUCH_DB_PASSWORD: [REDACTED:value]}
      COUCH_DB_URL: http://${COUCH_DB_USER}:[REDACTED:conn-password]@couchdb-service:5984
      INTERNAL_API_KEY: [REDACTED:value]}
      PLATFORM_URL: ${PLATFORM_URL}
      REDIS_URL: redis-service:6379
      REDIS_PASSWORD: [REDACTED:value]}
    depends_on:
      - redis-service
      - minio-service

  minio-service:
    restart: unless-stopped
    image: minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z
    volumes:
      - minio_data:/data
    environment:
      MINIO_ACCESS_KEY: [REDACTED:value]}
      MINIO_SECRET_KEY: [REDACTED:value]}
      MINIO_BROWSER: "off"
    command: server /data --console-address ":9001"
    healthcheck:
      test: "timeout 5s bash -c ':> /dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/9000' || exit 1"
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 20s
      retries: 3

  proxy-service:
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "10000:10000"
    container_name: bbproxy
    image: budibase/proxy:3.41.3
    environment:
      - PROXY_RATE_LIMIT_WEBHOOKS_PER_SECOND=10
      - PROXY_RATE_LIMIT_API_PER_SECOND=50
      - APPS_UPSTREAM_URL=http://app-service:4002
      - WORKER_UPSTREAM_URL=http://worker-service:4003
      - MINIO_UPSTREAM_URL=http://minio-service:9000
      - COUCHDB_UPSTREAM_URL=http://couchdb-service:5984
      - RESOLVER=[ip]
    depends_on:
      - minio-service
      - worker-service
      - app-service
      - couchdb-service

  couchdb-service:
    restart: unless-stopped
    image: budibase/database:2.1.0
    environment:
      - COUCHDB_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value]}
      - COUCHDB_USER=${COUCH_DB_USER}
      - TARGETBUILD=docker-compose
      - DATA_DIR=/data
    volumes:
      - couchdb3_data:/data

  redis-service:
    restart: unless-stopped
    image: redis:7.4.10
    command: redis-server --requirepass "${REDIS_PASSWORD}"
    volumes:
      - redis_data:/data

volumes:
  couchdb3_data:
    driver: local
  minio_data:
    driver: local
  redis_data:
    driver: local
